chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Recording for Verne, Coda, Muzak and Mercury in 1947
summary: He was recording steadily under several names, using numbers from Antobal's publishing house, Robbins, Chano and Guerra, plus Muzak instrumentals.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Okay, we are moving now toward the end of '47. Your Verne records are still getting a little air play in jukeboxes; I don't know about the radio. Ahh, you already have in the book, I believe, "Me dejan Solito", those things that you did for Tico later on and Continental. How did you get a hold of those number? Were they Robbins numbers also?
No, that was for (Marian) Sunshine, you know, Azpiazu?
.... Antobal.var. He had a publishing house and he had those numbers because his wife was ......
Yes. "Bejuco" was - ehh - belong to Chano Pozo, that was Robbins, and we had few from Marcelino Guerra that was Robbins.
Okay, you are recording with Verne. You are also recording for Coda under the name of Rene Hernandez. You did something under the name called "Conjunto Batiri". You did "La Toalla" ....
.... where Antar Daly was singing, right?; and you did something called- under the Afro-Cuban orchestra of - ahhh - Were you recording quite steadily at the time, at 1947?
Also, did Muzak come in at that time too?
Yes, and then Mercury. I think Muzak was a subsidy area of Mercury, something like that.
Yes, yeah, and we made - we made few with Muzak for that indirect music. We did a lot of instrumental for the indirect music.
Like "At Sundown" and "Hall of the Mambo King" and that?
Yeah, those are watered-down instrumental things. Yeah.
